build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player moves in a top-down view with WASD, aims with mouse, and attacks with click. Both player and enemies die in one hit, creating instant-death tension. Score 0 if there is no movement or combat.
A combo scoring system rewards chaining kills without pause — the multiplier increases with each rapid kill and decays or resets if the player hesitates. Score 0 if no combo system exists.

Doors can be interacted with (kicked open) to stun enemies behind them, and weapons can be picked up from the ground with limited ammo or single use. Score 0 if there are no interactive environment elements or weapon pickups.
Death instantly restarts the current floor with no loading screen, maintaining the die-and-retry flow. Score 0 if death ends the game or requires navigating menus to retry.
Enemies patrol set routes with visible awareness states; alerted enemies actively pursue and attack the player. Score 0 if enemies are static or have no AI behavior.
At least 8 distinct floor layouts with different room configurations, corridor arrangements, and enemy placements. Score 0 if only one floor exists.
At least 5 distinct weapon types with different behaviors (melee, pistol, shotgun, SMG, thrown) that force different tactical approaches. Score 0 if only one weapon exists.
At least 3 distinct enemy types with different behaviors (stationary guard, patrolling, armored, fast rusher) requiring different engagement strategies. Score 0 if only one enemy type exists.
Floor-clear scoring shows time, combo chain, weapon variety bonus, and overall grade with visible ranking. Score 0 if no scoring exists.
A campaign progression system tracks completed floors, best scores, and unlocks access to later floors. Score 0 if all floors are available from the start with no progression.
Normal startup shows a styled title screen with the game name, floor selection, and action-themed imagery. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The flow connects title to floor selection to gameplay to score screen without restarting the executable. Score 0 if major transitions are missing.
The HUD shows current combo multiplier, weapon and ammo count, and enemy count remaining in readable non-overlapping regions. Score 0 if the player cannot determine game state.

Player actions produce visible feedback: attacks show impact, kills spray effects, doors kicked show stun, combo increases flash, and death triggers a distinct animation. Score 0 if actions happen silently.

Art direction is coherent across title, floors, enemies, weapons, HUD, and score screens with a consistent gritty action palette and style. Score 0 if mostly default controls or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.
The player character, enemies, weapons, doors, and floor tiles use real sprite art with distinct designs. Score 0 if primary gameplay elements are unstyled rectangles.
Animation brings floors to life: enemy patrol animations, attack effects, door interactions, death sequences, and combo visual escalation. Score 0 if all elements are static.
HUD and UI panels use styled themed widgets with custom fonts, framed panels, or action-styled elements rather than raw HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if all UI is default Label/Button.
